September: The Golden Month

Ask any experienced UK motorcycle tourer their favourite month and September will be the most popular answer. The summer crowds vanish when schools return, the weather is often stable and warm, the light turns golden, and the landscape begins its autumn transformation. It's touring perfection.

Conditions

  • Temperature: Average 11-18°C. Indian summers can bring 22°C+. Mornings can be cool.
  • Daylight: 6:30am-7pm at the start, 7am-6:30pm by month's end. Still good riding hours.
  • Roads: Warm, dry tarmac. Less traffic than summer. Ideal conditions.

Why September Is Special

  • Empty roads: School return empties the tourist areas immediately. The contrast between August bank holiday and the first week of September is dramatic.
  • Autumn light: The lower sun creates warmer, more golden light. Landscapes glow in a way summer sun can't match.
  • Harvest time: Combine riding with harvest festivals, local food events, and seasonal produce.
  • Accommodation availability: Prices drop and availability improves. Spontaneous touring becomes possible again.

September Hazards

  • Shortening days: Don't get caught out by darkness. September sunsets come earlier each week.
  • Morning dew and mist: Cool nights create dew on roads and mist in valleys. Start your riding day slightly later or ride carefully through misty areas.
  • Falling leaves: Towards the end of September, deciduous trees start shedding. Wet leaves on roads are dangerously slippery.
  • Harvest machinery: Tractors and combine harvesters on rural roads. Be patient and overtake only when safe.

Where to Ride in September

  • Scottish Highlands: September is arguably the best month for Highland touring. No midges, warm days, spectacular autumn colours beginning in the birch woods.
  • Lake District: Peaceful after summer. The fells start turning gold and the lakes are mirror-calm on still mornings.
  • Snowdonia: Quiet roads, warm enough for mountain passes, and the oak woodlands beginning their colour change.
September is the month to take that tour you've been planning all year. Everything aligns — weather, traffic, light, landscape. If you do one multi-day tour a year, do it in September.

September Touring Recommendations

If you can take a week off in September, head to the Scottish Highlands. The combination of warm-ish weather, no midges, empty roads, and the first hints of autumn colour in the birch woodlands creates the single best touring experience of the UK year. The NC500, done slowly over 5-7 days in September, is magnificent.

Closer to home, the Lake District in September is peaceful and beautiful. The summer crowds evaporate when schools return, the fells start turning gold, and the lakes are mirror-calm on still mornings. An evening ride along Ullswater in September golden light is one of England's finest riding experiences.
